cvs: 'Mountain Fire' – bright red new growth · 'Katsura' – wine-red young leaves, pink flowers · 'Valley Valentine' – deep pink-red flowers · 'Debutante' – compact, upright flower sprays · 'Little Heath' – dwarf, variegated leaves
foliage: evergreen; glossy narrow leaves, scarlet when young, maturing to dark green
hardinessNote: Hardy in a cold winter throughout most of the UK, approximately -15 to -10°C, though new spring shoots can be scorched by late frost.
prune: Little needed. Lightly trim after flowering to remove spent flower sprays and cut any frost-damaged shoots back to healthy growth.
resilience: Hardy evergreen, but the new growth is scorched by late frost and cold wind. Needs acid soil and yellows on lime. Pests: Pieris lace bug, vine weevil; Phytophthora root rot in wet soil.
soilWarning: Shelter from cold wind and late frost
toxicity: All parts are toxic if eaten, especially the leaves and nectar. They can cause vomiting, drooling and a slowed heart rate in children, dogs, cats, horses and livestock.
uncertain: spelling: RHS lists the cultivar as 'Scarlett O'Hara'; many US nurseries spell it 'Scarlet'
height/spread: RHS gives 1.5–2.5 m; US nurseries quote up to 3–3.5 m, RHS used
hardiness: no RHS H-rating shown in search; H5 matches the species and the three Pieris cards in the deck (USDA 5–8)
compliance: not checked against a Xylella host list; no PBR known for this older cultivar
ratings and aspect: from the Forge draft and the deck's Pieris siblings, sunMin raised 25 -> 30 to sit with them
uses: Shrub borders · woodland gardens · ericaceous containers · shady patios
visual: Red young shoots in spring · drooping sprays of white bells on pink stalks · glossy evergreen
water: Water with rainwater in dry spells, especially the first summer and in pots. Mulch each spring to keep roots cool.
